a: A user-defined name of the function. Function names must be unique globally.
The runtime in which the function is going to run. Eg. "nodejs20", "python37", "go111".
Memory (in MB), available to the function. Default value is 256. Possible values include 128, 256, 512, 1024, etc.
A set of key/value environment variable pairs available during build time.
The fully-qualified name of the service account to be used for the build step of deploying this function
Name of the Cloud Build Custom Worker Pool that should be used to build the function.
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
Docker Registry to use for storing the function's Docker images. Allowed values are ARTIFACT_REGISTRY (default) and CONTAINER_REGISTRY.
User managed repository created in Artifact Registry optionally with a customer managed encryption key. If specified, deployments will use Artifact Registry for storing images built with Cloud Build.
Name of the function that will be executed when the Google Cloud Function is triggered.
A set of key/value environment variable pairs to assign to the function.
The security level for the function. Defaults to SECURE_OPTIONAL. Valid only if trigger_http is used.
URL which triggers function execution. Returned only if trigger_http is used.
String value that controls what traffic can reach the function. Allowed values are ALLOW_ALL and ALLOW_INTERNAL_ONLY. Changes to this field will recreate the cloud function.
Resource name of a KMS crypto key (managed by the user) used to encrypt/decrypt function resources.
A set of key/value label pairs to assign to the function. Label keys must follow the requirements at https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-labels#requirements.
The limit on the maximum number of function instances that may coexist at a given time.
The limit on the minimum number of function instances that may coexist at a given time.
Project of the function. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
Region of function. If it is not provided, the provider region is used.
If provided, the self-provided service account to run the function with.
The GCS bucket containing the zip archive which contains the function.
The source archive object (file) in archive bucket.
Timeout (in seconds) for the function. Default value is 60 seconds. Cannot be more than 540 seconds.

Boolean variable. Any HTTP request (of a supported type) to the endpoint will trigger function execution. Supported HTTP request types are: POST, PUT, GET, DELETE, and OPTIONS. Endpoint is returned as https_trigger_url.
The VPC Network Connector that this cloud function can connect to. It can be either the fully-qualified URI, or the short name of the network connector resource.
The egress settings for the connector, controlling what traffic is diverted through it. Allowed values are ALL_TRAFFIC and PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY. Defaults to PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY.
The type of event to observe. For example: "google.storage.object.finalize". See the documentation on calling Cloud Functions for a full reference of accepted triggers.
The name or partial URI of the resource from which to observe events. For example, "myBucket" or "projects/my-project/topics/my-topic"
Whether the function should be retried on failure. Defaults to false.
ID of the secret in secret manager (not the full resource name).

Version of the secret (version number or the string "latest"). It is recommended to use a numeric version for secret environment variables as any updates to the secret value is not reflected until new clones start.
Project identifier (due to a known limitation, only project number is supported by this field) of the project that contains the secret.
The path within the container to mount the secret volume. For example, setting the mount_path as "/etc/secrets" would mount the secret value files under the "/etc/secrets" directory.
ID of the secret in secret manager (not the full resource name).
Project identifier (due to a known limitation, only project number is supported by this field) of the project that contains the secret.
Relative path of the file under the mount path where the secret value for this version will be fetched and made available.
Version of the secret (version number or the string "latest"). It is preferable to use "latest" version with secret volumes as secret value changes are reflected immediately.
The URL pointing to the hosted repository where the function is defined.
